# SSHGate classifier corpus.
# Format: <EXPECTED>\t<cmd>
# EXPECTED: READ or WRITE. Comment lines (#) and blank lines are ignored.
# Sourced verbatim from spec §"Command Classification".

# --- Read list (auto-allowed) ---
READ	cat /etc/hosts

# --- Tricky / classification-rule cases ---
# Pipes: if ANY segment is a write, the whole thing is a write.
WRITE	ps aux | tee /tmp/x
READ	cat /etc/hosts | grep foo
READ	ls -la | head -n 5
WRITE	cat /etc/hosts | tee /tmp/copy
# Redirects (>, >>) → write.
WRITE	echo hi > /tmp/x
WRITE	cat /etc/hosts >> /tmp/dump
READ	cat </dev/zero | head -c 10
# Semicolons / && / ||: any write segment → write.
WRITE	ls; rm -f /tmp/x
READ	ls && echo done
WRITE	ls && rm /tmp/x
WRITE	ls || rm /tmp/x
# sudo prefix → always write, regardless of what follows.
WRITE	sudo cat /etc/hosts
WRITE	sudo ls /root
# curl with -X POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH or -d/--data → write; bare curl → read.
WRITE	curl -X POST https://example.com/api
WRITE	curl -X PUT https://example.com/api
WRITE	curl -X DELETE https://example.com/api
WRITE	curl -X PATCH https://example.com/api
WRITE	curl -d "k=v" https://example.com
WRITE	curl --data "k=v" https://example.com
# Unknown commands default to write.
WRITE	frobnicate --foo
WRITE	madeupbinary arg1 arg2

# --- v1.1 Task B: refined pipe/chain segment classification ---
# All-read pipelines/chains are now READ (v1 used to flag these as WRITE).
READ	cat /etc/hosts | grep foo
READ	ps aux | head -5
READ	ls /tmp | wc -l
READ	journalctl -u nginx | tail -20
READ	df -h ; free -m
READ	uptime && uname -a
READ	cat /tmp/x|grep foo
# Output redirects keep the chain a WRITE even if every command in it is a read.
WRITE	cat /etc/hosts > /tmp/copy
WRITE	echo hi | tee -a /tmp/foo
# Command and process substitution are opaque → fail-safe WRITE.
WRITE	ls $(rm /tmp/x)
WRITE	echo `whoami`
WRITE	diff <(ls /a) <(ls /b)
WRITE	tee >(cat) < /dev/null

# --- v1.1 Task B: tightened git/wget/curl rules (Mi3, Mi4) ---
WRITE	git stash
WRITE	git stash push
WRITE	git stash pop
WRITE	git restore main.go
WRITE	git switch main
WRITE	git config --set user.name alice
READ	git stash list
READ	git stash show stash@{0}
READ	git config --get user.name
WRITE	wget https://example.com/file.tar
READ	wget -O- https://example.com/cfg
READ	wget --output-document=- https://example.com/cfg
WRITE	curl -o /tmp/x https://example.com
WRITE	curl --output /tmp/x https://example.com
READ	curl https://example.com/api/status

# --- 2026-05-19 read-only-gate bypass BLOCKERs (security research audit) ---
# B1: sed `e` flag / `w`/`r`/`R` commands execute shell or write files.
WRITE	sed 's/.*/id/e'
WRITE	sed -e 's/X/Y/e' /etc/hosts
WRITE	sed 's/X/Y/w /tmp/log' file
WRITE	sed '1r /etc/passwd' file
# B1 — simple-reader sed forms still pass.
READ	sed 's/foo/bar/' /etc/hosts

# B2: find `-fprint*`, `-fls`, `-ok*` write files or exec commands.
WRITE	find /tmp -fprintf /etc/passwd 'evil\n'
WRITE	find /tmp -fprint /tmp/list
WRITE	find /tmp -fls /tmp/list
WRITE	find /tmp -fprint0 /tmp/list
WRITE	find /tmp -ok rm {} \;
# B2 — simple find readers still pass.
READ	find /tmp -name '*.log'
READ	find /tmp -name '*.log' -print

# B3: env-var smuggling — dangerous KEY=VAL prefixes force WRITE.
WRITE	GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF='sh -c "id"' git log -p
WRITE	GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o ProxyCommand=...' git ls-remote origin
WRITE	LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/evil.so cat /etc/hosts
WRITE	IFS=$'\n' ls /etc
WRITE	PATH=/tmp ls
WRITE	PYTHONSTARTUP=/tmp/evil.py python -c "print(1)"

# B4: awk `system()`, `getline`, pipe-to-cmd, redirect-to-file → WRITE.
WRITE	awk 'BEGIN{system("rm /tmp/x")}'
WRITE	awk 'BEGIN{getline x; print x}' /etc/hosts
WRITE	awk '{print | "rm /tmp/x"}' file
WRITE	awk '{print > "/tmp/log"}' file
# B4 — simple awk readers still pass.
READ	awk '{print $1}' /etc/passwd
READ	awk '/^root/ {print $1}' /etc/passwd

# --- 2026-05-19 read-only-gate bypass MAJORs (security research audit) ---
# M1: `env <cmd>` wrapper bypass. `env` alone is read; `env KEY=VAL` is read;
# `env KEY=VAL cmd args...` recursively classifies the wrapped command; any
# env flag (-i, -u, -S, --ignore-environment, etc.) forces WRITE.
WRITE	env rm /tmp/x
WRITE	env -i rm /tmp/x
WRITE	env -u PATH rm /tmp/x
WRITE	env --ignore-environment rm /tmp/x
WRITE	env LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/evil.so cat /etc/hosts
WRITE	env GIT_SSH_COMMAND='sh -c "id"' git ls-remote origin
WRITE	env -- rm /tmp/x
READ	env
READ	env FOO=bar
READ	env FOO=bar cat /etc/hosts
READ	env FOO=bar ls /tmp
READ	env LANG=C printenv PATH

# M2: journalctl mutating flags (--rotate, --vacuum-*, --flush, --update-catalog,
# --setup-keys, --relinquish-var, --smart-relinquish-var, --sync) force WRITE,
# including GNU long-option abbreviations.
WRITE	journalctl --rotate
WRITE	journalctl --vacuum-size=100M
WRITE	journalctl --vacuum-time=7d
WRITE	journalctl --vacuum-files=10
WRITE	journalctl --flush
WRITE	journalctl --sync
WRITE	journalctl --relinquish-var
WRITE	journalctl --smart-relinquish-var
WRITE	journalctl --update-catalog
WRITE	journalctl --setup-keys
WRITE	journalctl --rot
WRITE	journalctl --vacu
WRITE	journalctl --flu
# M2 — simple journalctl readers still pass.
READ	journalctl -u nginx --since "1 hour ago"
READ	journalctl -xe
READ	journalctl --no-pager -u nginx

# M3: `git -c KEY=VAL ...` injects config (core.pager, alias.*, diff.external,
# core.sshCommand, gpg.program, etc.) — all reach a shell. Conservative: any
# `-c` arg forces WRITE.
WRITE	git -c core.pager='sh -c "id"' log
WRITE	git -c alias.x='!id' x
WRITE	git -c core.sshCommand='evil' fetch
WRITE	git -c core.editor='vim' status
WRITE	git --config-env=core.pager=ENV log
# M3 — bare git read forms still pass.
READ	git log --oneline
READ	git status

# M4: GNU long-option abbreviation. sed `--in-pl`, `--in`, `--in-p` all
# expand to `--in-place` and mutate the file. journalctl `--rot` / `--vacu`
# / `--flu` expand to their dangerous canonical forms (covered above in M2).
WRITE	sed --in-place 's/X/Y/' /etc/hosts
WRITE	sed --in-pl 's/X/Y/' /etc/hosts
WRITE	sed --in-p 's/X/Y/' /etc/hosts
WRITE	sed --in 's/X/Y/' /etc/hosts
WRITE	sed --in-place=.bak 's/X/Y/' /etc/hosts

# M5: curl `-K FILE` / `--config FILE` reads directives from FILE; the file
# can specify any curl arg including `--output FILE` or `-T FILE`.
WRITE	curl -K /tmp/cfg https://example.com
WRITE	curl --config /tmp/cfg https://example.com
WRITE	curl --config=/tmp/cfg https://example.com
# M5 — bare curl read still passes.
READ	curl https://example.com/status

# --- sed long-option prefix and git config-through-environment ---
WRITE	sed --i 's/X/Y/' /etc/hosts
WRITE	sed --i=.bak 's/X/Y/' /etc/hosts
WRITE	GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.fsmonitor=id'" git status
WRITE	GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=diff.external GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=id git diff HEAD~1
WRITE	GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/tmp/x git log
WRITE	env GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.pager=id'" git log
WRITE	EDITOR=id git log
WRITE	SYSTEMD_PAGER=id systemctl status nginx
WRITE	GIT_TRACE=/etc/x git status
WRITE	GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=id git log
WRITE	LD_DEBUG_OUTPUT=/etc/x ls
READ	sed -n '1,5p' /etc/hosts
READ	git status
